Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Semiconductor contact architectures are provided, wherein contact metal extends into the semiconductor layer to which contact is being made, thereby increasing contact area. An offset spacer allows a relatively deep etch into the semiconductor material to be achieved. Thus, rather than just a flat horizontal surface of the semiconductor being exposed for contact area, relatively long vertical trench sidewalls and a bottom wall are exposed and available for contact area. The trench can then be filled with the desired contact metal. Doping of the semiconductor layer into which the contact is being formed can be carried out in a manner that facilitates an efficient contact trench etch process, such as by, for example, utilization of post trench etch doping or a semiconductor layer having an upper undoped region through which the contact trench etch passes and a lower doped S/D region. The offset spacer may be removed from final structure.

The contact metal extends into the semiconductor layer, thereby increasing the available contact area between the metal and the semiconductor. An offset spacer facilitates the formation of a relatively deep trench in the semiconductor material. Unlike a conventional contact formed only on a flat horizontal surface, the trench exposes vertical sidewalls as well as a bottom wall, providing additional surfaces for electrical contact.

After etching, the trench can be filled with the desired contact metal to form an embedded contact structure. Efficient trench formation may be achieved by doping the semiconductor after the etch or by providing an upper undoped region above a lower doped source/drain region. These approaches can improve control of the trench-etching process while preserving the desired electrical characteristics. Once the trench has been formed, the offset spacer may optionally be removed.
outputs.L4:
A semiconductor contact architecture may be formed by increasing the interfacial area between a conductive contact and an underlying semiconductor layer. Rather than placing the contact only on a substantially planar upper surface, an offset spacer is used as an etch mask to define one or more deep trenches in the semiconductor material. The trenches extend downward from the upper surface and expose both vertical semiconductor sidewalls and a lower semiconductor surface. When filled with a conductive contact material, these additional surfaces create a three-dimensional contact interface having substantially greater area than a conventional flat contact of the same lateral footprint.

In an example fabrication process, a doped source/drain region is formed in or over a semiconductor body. An offset spacer is then positioned adjacent to a gate structure, masking feature, or other device element. The spacer establishes the lateral separation between that element and the trench to be formed. An anisotropic etch removes exposed portions of the semiconductor layer and produces a trench with relatively deep, generally vertical sidewalls. The trench depth, width, number, and spacing may be selected according to the desired contact resistance, device dimensions, and process limitations.

The semiconductor exposed by the trench may be doped after etching. For example, dopant species may be introduced into the trench sidewalls and bottom by implantation, diffusion, plasma doping, or another suitable technique. Post-etch doping can increase the carrier concentration at the contact interface and thereby reduce contact resistance. An activation treatment may subsequently be performed if required.

In another embodiment, the semiconductor layer initially includes an undoped or more lightly doped upper region positioned above a doped source/drain region. The trench etch passes through at least part of the upper region and exposes the underlying doped material. The contact can therefore engage the doped source/drain region along the trench bottom and, depending on the trench depth and layer configuration, along portions of the trench sidewalls. This arrangement may simplify control of the original doping profile while still providing a large, low-resistance contact interface.

After trench formation and any optional doping or surface treatment, the trenches are filled with contact metal or another conductive material. Suitable processing may include deposition of an interface layer, a barrier or liner, and a conductive fill. The conductive material may also extend over the upper surface to connect the trench-filled regions to an interconnect structure. Excess material can be removed or patterned using planarization and etching processes.

The offset spacer may serve only as a temporary fabrication feature. Once the trench location and geometry have been established, the spacer can be removed so that it is absent from the completed device. Alternatively, removal may occur after one or more subsequent processing operations, provided that the trench and nearby structures remain protected.

Because the conductive fill contacts the semiconductor along the trench sidewalls as well as the trench bottom, the effective contact area can be much larger than that of a planar interface occupying the same device footprint. The enlarged interface can lower electrical contact resistance, improve current injection and extraction, and support efficient device operation without requiring a corresponding increase in lateral contact dimensions. The architecture is therefore particularly useful in highly scaled semiconductor devices, where available surface area is limited but low-resistance source/drain contacts remain important.

### Semiconductor Technology

The semiconductor is the foundation of modern electronics. Semiconductor materials, such as silicon, can control the flow of electricity, making them essential for manufacturing transistors, microprocessors, sensors, and memory chips. Their unique properties enable electronic devices to process information efficiently while remaining compact and energy-efficient.

The growing demand for smartphones, computers, electric vehicles, and artificial intelligence has made semiconductor production strategically important worldwide. counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention that uses an offset spacer to enable deep contact trench etching, exposing vertical sidewalls and a bottom surface for improved source/drain contacts.
counterfactuals.output: The invention forms an offset spacer next to a transistor gate to separate and protect the gate during a deep contact-trench etch. The trench extends beside the source/drain region, exposing both its vertical sidewalls and bottom surface. A conductive material then fills the trench, creating a larger, multi-surface source/drain contact. This structure improves contact area, lowers electrical resistance, and supports tighter device scaling while reducing the risk of gate-to-contact shorts.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical paragraph explaining how recessed semiconductor contacts can reduce contact resistance through increased metal-to-semiconductor interface area, including suitable doping strategies.
counterfactuals.output: Recessed semiconductor contacts reduce effective contact resistance by extending the metal–semiconductor junction from a planar surface onto the recess sidewalls and, where applicable, the recess floor, thereby increasing the electrically active interface area and distributing current over a larger perimeter. The shorter access path and reduced current crowding can further lower the total resistance, provided that recess etching does not introduce excessive surface damage or interface states. To minimize the specific contact resistivity, the semiconductor beneath and around the recess should be degenerately doped, for example using a self-aligned high-dose ion implant followed by activation annealing, in-situ doped epitaxial regrowth, or a thin delta-doped layer near the interface. Selecting the appropriate n-type or p-type dopant and maintaining a steep doping profile confines the highly doped region to the contact area, narrowing the Schottky barrier and promoting tunneling while avoiding mobility degradation, leakage, or threshold-voltage shifts in the active channel.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a semiconductor fabrication method involving contact trench formation, optional post-etch doping, an upper undoped region above a doped source/drain region, and subsequent offset-spacer removal.
counterfactuals.output:
A semiconductor fabrication method can include the following sequence:

1. Form a gate structure over a semiconductor body and provide removable offset spacers along the gate sidewalls.
2. Form doped source/drain regions adjacent to the gate while retaining an upper semiconductor region above each source/drain region that is substantially undoped or more lightly doped.
3. Deposit an interlayer dielectric and etch a contact trench through the dielectric and the upper undoped region, thereby exposing or extending into the underlying doped source/drain region.
4. Optionally perform a post-etch doping step, such as angled or vertical ion implantation, plasma doping, or diffusion, to dope exposed trench surfaces and reduce contact resistance.
5. After forming the contact trench, selectively remove the offset spacers, for example through the trench or through an associated opening, without substantially attacking the gate dielectric or surrounding dielectric.
6. Deposit a liner and/or contact metal into the trench and any space created by offset-spacer removal, followed by planarization to form the source/drain contact.

The upper undoped region protects or separates the doped source/drain during earlier processing, while the trench etch and optional post-etch doping provide a low-resistance electrical connection.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

## Exemplary Title

**Transistor Contact Structure Having a Recessed Source/Drain Contact Defined Using a Temporary Offset Spacer**

## Abstract

A semiconductor device and a method of forming the same are disclosed. The method includes forming a source/drain semiconductor region adjacent to a gate structure and forming a temporary offset spacer that covers a first portion of the source/drain semiconductor region while exposing a second portion thereof. An etching process removes semiconductor material from the exposed second portion to form a contact trench extending into the source/drain semiconductor region. A dimension and/or etch characteristic of the temporary offset spacer is selected to control a depth and a lateral position of the contact trench. The temporary offset spacer may comprise a material having a predetermined etch rate in the etching process, thereby providing an etch-budget indicator or sacrificial depth-control feature. After the contact trench is formed, at least a portion of the temporary offset spacer is removed, and a contact metal is deposited in the contact trench such that the contact metal penetrates below an original upper surface of the source/drain semiconductor region. The recessed contact arrangement can reduce contact resistance while permitting an efficient, self-aligned etching process.

## Exemplary Independent Device Claim

1. **A semiconductor device, comprising:**
   
   a substrate;
   
   a gate structure disposed over a channel region of the substrate;
   
   a source/drain semiconductor region adjacent to the channel region, the source/drain semiconductor region having an upper surface; and
   
   a conductive contact comprising a contact metal extending through the upper surface and into the source/drain semiconductor region to a bottom contact interface located below the upper surface,
   
   wherein the conductive contact includes a lower portion embedded within the source/drain semiconductor region and an upper portion electrically coupled to an interconnect structure, and
   
   wherein the lower portion is laterally offset from the gate structure by an offset distance corresponding to a lateral dimension of a temporary offset spacer used during formation of the conductive contact.

## Exemplary Independent Method Claim

2. **A method of forming a semiconductor device, comprising:**
   
   forming a gate structure over a channel region;
   
   forming a source/drain semiconductor region adjacent to the gate structure;
   
   forming a temporary offset spacer that masks a first portion of the source/drain semiconductor region and exposes a second portion of the source/drain semiconductor region;
   
   etching the exposed second portion of the source/drain semiconductor region to form a contact trench extending below an original upper surface of the source/drain semiconductor region, wherein at least one of a thickness, a height, a composition, or an etch rate of the temporary offset spacer is selected to control a depth of the contact trench;
   
   removing at least a portion of the temporary offset spacer; and
   
   depositing a contact metal in the contact trench such that the contact metal extends into the source/drain semiconductor region.

## Exemplary Independent Process Claim Emphasizing Etch Efficiency

3. **A method, comprising:**
   
   providing a transistor structure including a gate structure and an epitaxial source/drain region;
   
   depositing a sacrificial spacer material adjacent to the gate structure;
   
   patterning the sacrificial spacer material to form a temporary offset spacer over a portion of the epitaxial source/drain region;
   
   performing a common etching process that etches an exposed portion of the epitaxial source/drain region and consumes at least part of the temporary offset spacer, the temporary offset spacer having a predetermined consumption rate correlated with a target penetration depth in the epitaxial source/drain region;
   
   terminating the common etching process based on consumption of a predetermined amount of the temporary offset spacer, thereby forming a contact recess having the target penetration depth;
   
   removing residual sacrificial spacer material; and
   
   forming a conductive material in the contact recess.

## Dependent Claims

4. The semiconductor device of claim 1, wherein the bottom contact interface is spaced below the upper surface of the source/drain semiconductor region by between about 2 nm and about 50 nm.

5. The semiconductor device of claim 1, wherein the source/drain semiconductor region comprises epitaxial silicon, silicon germanium, silicon carbide, germanium, or a III-V semiconductor material.

6. The semiconductor device of claim 1, wherein the contact metal comprises tungsten, cobalt, ruthenium, molybdenum, titanium, tantalum, nickel, copper, or a combination thereof.

7. The semiconductor device of claim 1, further comprising a metal-semiconductor compound disposed between the contact metal and the source/drain semiconductor region.

8. The semiconductor device of claim 7, wherein the metal-semiconductor compound comprises a silicide, a germanosilicide, or a germanide.

9. The semiconductor device of claim 1, wherein the lower portion of the conductive contact has a width less than a width of the upper portion.

10. The semiconductor device of claim 1, wherein the conductive contact is separated from the gate structure by a permanent gate spacer, and the offset distance is greater than or equal to a lateral thickness of the permanent gate spacer.

11. The method of claim 2, wherein the temporary offset spacer comprises silicon oxide, silicon nitride, silicon oxynitride, silicon carbide, amorphous carbon, an organic material, or a multilayer combination thereof.

12. The method of claim 2, wherein etching the exposed second portion comprises an anisotropic plasma etching process.

13. The method of claim 2, wherein etching the exposed second portion comprises a cyclic process including an etchant exposure operation and a removal operation.

14. The method of claim 2, wherein the temporary offset spacer functions as both a lateral etch mask and a sacrificial etch-budget structure.

15. The method of claim 2, wherein the temporary offset spacer is formed with a thickness selected to establish a minimum lateral separation between the contact trench and the gate structure.

16. The method of claim 2, wherein the temporary offset spacer has a known etch-rate ratio relative to the source/drain semiconductor region, and the depth of the contact trench is controlled based on the known etch-rate ratio and an initial dimension of the temporary offset spacer.

17. The method of claim 2, further comprising detecting an endpoint associated with exposure, thinning, or removal of a portion of the temporary offset spacer.

18. The method of claim 2, wherein the etching is performed using a chemistry selected to remove the source/drain semiconductor region at a higher rate than a gate dielectric, a permanent gate spacer, or an interlayer dielectric.

19. The method of claim 2, further comprising cleaning a semiconductor surface within the contact trench and forming an interfacial metal layer before depositing the contact metal.

20. The method of claim 2, further comprising annealing the interfacial metal layer to form a metal-semiconductor compound along sidewall and bottom surfaces of the contact trench.

21. The method of claim 2, wherein removing the temporary offset spacer increases an opening width above the contact trench before depositing the contact metal.

22. The method of claim 21, wherein the increased opening width reduces an aspect ratio of a contact opening and facilitates void-free deposition of the contact metal.

23. The method of claim 3, wherein the common etching process uses a plasma chemistry comprising a halogen-containing species.

24. The method of claim 3, wherein the target penetration depth is controlled without a separate lithographic patterning operation directed to the contact recess.

25. The method of claim 3, wherein the temporary offset spacer is removed selectively relative to a permanent gate spacer and an interlayer dielectric.

## Exemplary Specification Language

In some embodiments, a temporary offset spacer is formed adjacent to a gate stack before etching a contact recess into a source/drain semiconductor region. The temporary offset spacer may cover a gate-proximal portion of the source/drain semiconductor region and expose a gate-distal portion. Accordingly, the temporary offset spacer establishes a controlled lateral separation between the subsequently formed contact recess and the gate stack, reducing the likelihood of gate-to-contact shorting.

The temporary offset spacer may additionally provide depth control. For example, the spacer material and its initial thickness or height may be selected such that the spacer is consumed at a predictable rate during etching of the source/drain semiconductor region. Consumption of a predetermined portion of the spacer may correspond to removal of a predetermined thickness of the source/drain semiconductor material. Spacer consumption may therefore provide a physical etch budget, an endpoint-detection signal, or both. In other embodiments, the spacer remains substantially intact and controls recess depth indirectly by defining the exposed area, local etch loading, ion trajectory, or etchant transport to the source/drain semiconductor region.

After formation of the contact recess, the temporary offset spacer may be removed to enlarge an upper portion of the contact opening. This sequence permits the semiconductor recess to be etched through a relatively narrow, self-aligned opening while permitting conductive material to be deposited through a wider opening. The enlarged opening can reduce deposition aspect ratio, improve precursor transport, and reduce seam or void formation.

A liner, adhesion layer, barrier layer, or silicidation metal may be deposited along the bottom and sidewalls of the contact recess. A thermal treatment may form a metal-semiconductor compound at the recessed contact interface. A conductive fill material is then deposited such that at least a portion of the conductive fill material is positioned below the original upper surface of the source/drain semiconductor region. The resulting increased contact-interface area and reduced current path through the source/drain region may lower contact resistance.
